review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the other files in the SolidTorusNeighborhood directory for uses of the open solid torus set and of `SolidTorus`. I also looked at `cross_orthonormal`. I did not examine the linear-isometry bundling of `ψ` in the same depth. It is a private, single-use lemma, so I reported it as a lower-confidence finding. The `IsSolidTorusNeighborhood` structure and `boundaryInclusion` looked reasonable. A bundled topological embedding type for `boundaryInclusion` does not exist in Mathlib, so I did not propose one.

findings.problem: The open solid torus, the interior of `D² × S¹`, is never named. It is written out as `{p : SolidTorus | ‖(p.1 : ℂ)‖ < 1}` in the structure field and in `closure_setOf_norm_lt_one`, `range_subset_image`, `frontier_image` and `exteriorFrontierHomeomorph`. This file has 6 occurrences and the sibling files have 9 more (`Exterior.lean`, `Link/Basic.lean`, `Link/Exterior.lean`). The boundary torus does have a name (`boundaryInclusion`, `range_boundaryInclusion`), so the two parts of the solid torus are treated asymmetrically. The theorem `closure_setOf_norm_lt_one` is just a lemma about this unnamed set. `knotExterior` and `linkExterior` each re-spell it inside their own definitions.
findings.proposed_change: Add `def SolidTorus.openPart : Set SolidTorus := {p | ‖(p.1 : ℂ)‖ < 1}` (the name is a suggestion), with `mem_openPart`, `isOpen_openPart` and `closure_openPart` (the current `closure_setOf_norm_lt_one`). Use it in the field `isOpen_image : IsOpen (Φ '' SolidTorus.openPart)`, in `frontier_image`, in `exteriorFrontierHomeomorph`, and in the downstream `knotExterior`/`linkExterior` definitions. Keep `range_boundaryInclusion` as the dual statement. If the `{p | ‖…‖ < 1}` form must stay usable by `simp`, state `mem_openPart` as a `simp` lemma.
findings.benefit: The definition of `IsSolidTorusNeighborhood`, which is the central notion of the file, would read as 'the image of the open solid torus is open'. The open and boundary parts of the solid torus become symmetric named objects. Downstream files stop duplicating the set-builder and its membership proofs. The openness of the set is proved once, where it is currently re-derived at each use.

findings.excerpt: ∃ ψ : Circle → ℂ → ℝ³, Continuous (fun q : SolidTorus => ψ q.2 q.1) ∧ ∀ z,
findings.problem: The docstring says `ψ z` is a 'continuous family of linear isometries onto the normal planes', but the statement uses a bare function `ψ : Circle → ℂ → ℝ³`. It lists the isometry properties as separate conjuncts: `‖ψ z w‖ = ‖w‖`, `Injective (ψ z)`, membership in `normalSubspace`, and surjectivity onto it. Linearity is never stated, and the proof of injectivity is done by hand with `Complex.ext` and `h₁`/`h₂`. Injectivity of an isometry is a standard consequence that Mathlib already supplies for `ℂ →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³`.
findings.proposed_change: Produce `ψ : Circle → ℂ →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³` with `Continuous (fun q : SolidTorus => ψ q.2 q.1)` and `∀ z, LinearMap.range (ψ z).toLinearMap = normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z`, or the equivalent pointwise range statement. Construct each `ψ z` from the frame `n₁ z, n₂ z` through its coordinates `re` and `im`. The consumer then gets `norm_map` and `LinearIsometry.injective` for free, so the norm and `Injective` conjuncts and the manual `Complex.ext` argument disappear. In `exists_isSolidTorusNeighborhood`, `hnorm` becomes `norm_smul` plus `LinearIsometry.norm_map`. This is a lower-confidence suggestion, since the lemma is private and has a single consumer. The extra `map_add`/`map_smul` proofs partly offset the saving.
findings.benefit: The linear and isometric structure is exposed in the type instead of being scattered across conjuncts. Injectivity, and possibly the norm computation, come from library lemmas rather than a bespoke proof. The statement matches its own docstring.
